title: Medline BioCon 700 / 750 Series Bladder Scanner - Probe / Scan Head Connection Failure
description: Troubleshooting an absent, intermittent, or unreliable probe connection caused by seating, connector contamination, cable damage, probe failure, or scanner-side faults.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unresolved probe or scan-head connection failure while relying on the BioCon scanner for a clinical bladder-volume assessment. Move the patient to another verified bladder scanner or appropriate clinical assessment method before continuing. Expected: Patient care is not dependent on a scanner with an unreliable probe connection. Why it matters: The BioCon platform depends on the ultrasound probe to acquire the information required for bladder-volume measurement. Medline identifies a replacement probe specifically for the BioCon 700 and 750 platforms. If transferring to another device resolves the immediate clinical concern, continue troubleshooting only in a controlled Clinical Engineering setting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure Behavior
steps.instructions: Power on the scanner and determine what Clinical Engineering can reproduce: Probe not detected; No scan response when scanning is initiated; Intermittent probe recognition; Connection lost when the cable is moved; Absent or abnormal prescan image; Failure only after startup; Hardware, maintenance, or self-diagnostic indication; Device recognizes the probe but scanning remains abnormal. Document the exact behavior rather than recording only “probe bad.” Expected: The complaint is narrowed to a reproducible connection, cable, probe, or scanner-side symptom. If the probe operates normally and repeated scans are stable, the issue may have been transient. Document testing and stop.

steps.title: 3. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: Shut down the scanner normally. Allow the device to fully power down, then restart it and observe whether the probe is recognized consistently. Expected: The probe initializes and remains available after startup. Why it matters: A controlled restart helps distinguish a temporary initialization or communication problem from a repeatable hardware fault. If restart restores normal operation, perform repeated functional scans before returning the device to service. If the issue does not recur and testing passes, document the result and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Probe and Scan Head Externally
steps.instructions: Examine the complete probe assembly for: Cracked housing; Separation at seams; Impact damage; Loose components; Signs of fluid intrusion; Damaged strain relief; Cable cuts or crushing; Severe twisting or kinking; Unusual heat; Burnt odor; Evidence of improper cleaning or chemical damage. Do not continue using a visibly compromised probe. Expected: The probe housing and cable are intact with no obvious condition that could compromise reliable operation. Medline markets a dedicated replacement probe for the BioCon 700 and 750, supporting probe substitution as an appropriate external troubleshooting step rather than assuming immediate console failure. If physical damage is found, remove the affected probe or scanner from service as appropriate and stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Probe Connection Point
steps.instructions: With the device safely removed from patient use, inspect the accessible probe connection area. Check for: Incomplete seating; Loose connection; Debris; Dried gel; Cleaning residue; Moisture; Bent or damaged accessible contacts; Cracked connector housing; Mechanical looseness. Do not insert metal objects into the connector and do not force a damaged connection. Expected: The connection area is clean, dry, mechanically intact, and capable of secure engagement. If contamination is present, clean only according to approved facility and manufacturer-compatible practices, allow the area to dry fully, reconnect, and retest. If this restores stable probe recognition, document the corrective action and stop.

steps.title: 6. Disconnect and Reseat the Probe Connection Where User-Accessible
steps.instructions: If the installed configuration provides a user-accessible probe connection, disconnect it only after the scanner is safely powered down and removed from clinical use. Inspect the connection, then reconnect it fully without forcing it. Restart the scanner and check recognition. Expected: The probe is consistently recognized after proper reseating. If reseating resolves the issue, perform repeated functional checks and stop once reliable operation is verified. If the connection is not intended for routine user or field disconnection, do not force access or proceed into internal disassembly.

steps.title: 7. Check for Cable-Position Sensitivity
steps.instructions: With the scanner in a controlled bench setting, observe operation while gently repositioning the probe cable through normal ranges of movement. Pay particular attention near: Probe strain relief; Connector strain relief; Areas showing previous compression; Frequently flexed cable sections. Do not sharply bend, twist, or stress the cable. Expected: Probe recognition and scanning remain stable during ordinary cable positioning. If recognition repeatedly drops at a particular cable position, suspect an intermittent probe cable or connection fault. Remove the affected assembly from service and stop.

steps.title: 8. Test With a Known-Good Compatible Probe
steps.instructions: When an approved known-good BioCon 700/750-compatible probe is available, substitute it for comparison. Medline lists a replacement probe for the BioCon 700 and 750 bladder scanners, making controlled probe substitution a strong isolation step. Retest: Startup recognition; Scan initiation; Prescan behavior where applicable; Repeated scan stability; Cable-position stability. Expected: A known-good compatible probe operates consistently. Interpret the result logically: Known-good probe works: Original probe or cable assembly is strongly suspect. Known-good probe also fails: Scanner-side connector, communication, or internal hardware becomes more likely. Both probes are intermittent: Investigate scanner-side connection integrity and escalate. If the known-good probe resolves the problem and required functional testing passes, replace or quarantine the defective probe, document the result, and stop.

steps.title: 9. Cross-Test the Suspect Probe When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If another compatible, verified BioCon 700/750 unit is available and facility procedures permit, test the suspect probe on that known-good platform. Expected: The cross-test helps determine whether the problem follows the probe. Interpretation: Failure follows the probe: Probe or cable assembly is likely defective. Probe works normally on another compatible unit: Original scanner-side connection or internal circuitry becomes more likely. Results remain inconsistent: Remove the questionable equipment from service pending further evaluation. Do not use a patient to perform comparative troubleshooting.

steps.title: 10. Evaluate Scan Function After Connection Is Restored
steps.instructions: A probe that is merely “detected” should not automatically be considered functional. After stable recognition is restored, verify appropriate operation using an approved functional-check method, test object, phantom, or facility procedure. For the BioCon 700, Medline lists a calibration kit among available accessories. Check for: Stable scan initiation; Repeatable acquisition; Reasonable image or targeting behavior; No connection dropouts; No abnormal hardware indications; Consistent repeated results under the approved test method. Expected: The probe remains connected and the scanner performs repeatably. If connection is restored but functional performance remains abnormal, do not return the scanner to service solely because the probe is detected.

steps.title: 11. Review Self-Diagnostic or Hardware Indications
steps.instructions: If the scanner displays a hardware, maintenance, or diagnostic indication, record the exact message and determine whether it persists with: Restart; Connection reseating; Known-good compatible probe; Verified external condition. The BioCon 750 is described as providing built-in self-diagnostic capability intended to alert users to hardware or maintenance issues. Expected: A transient external issue clears after correction; a repeatable diagnostic fault remains reproducible. Do not repeatedly clear or ignore a persistent hardware indication.

steps.title: 12. Perform Final Reproducibility Testing
steps.instructions: Before return to service, complete several repeated functional cycles. Verify: Probe recognized after startup; No intermittent disconnect; Scan command responds normally; Functional test is repeatable; Cable movement within normal handling does not interrupt operation; No abnormal messages; No unusual heat, odor, or sound. Expected: The scanner performs consistently across repeated tests. If the issue recurs even once during final testing, do not return the device to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the BioCon 750 intermittently failed to recognize the scan probe and would not reliably initiate bladder scans.
CCR.Cause: Inspection and substitution testing found that the connection failure followed the original probe assembly, while a known-good compatible probe remained stable.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the defective probe from service, installed a verified compatible replacement probe, completed repeated functional scans without disconnects, and returned the scanner to service.

helpfulDetails: Functional test or approved phantom check completed

title: Medline BioCon 700 / 750 Series Bladder Scanner - Battery Not Charging or Short Runtime
description: Troubleshooting failed charging, low battery endurance, rapid discharge, inconsistent charge indication, or suspected battery and external power problems.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unresolved battery or power problem while the bladder scanner is being relied upon for active clinical assessment. Move the affected scanner away from patient use and provide clinical staff with another verified bladder scanner when needed. Expected: Patient care is not dependent on equipment with uncertain battery availability. Why it matters: An unexpected shutdown can interrupt scanning and create uncertainty about whether the device is ready for continued clinical use. If removing the affected scanner resolves the immediate clinical concern, continue troubleshooting only in a controlled Clinical Engineering setting.

steps.title: Confirm the Exact Reported Failure
steps.instructions: Determine what “battery not charging” or “short runtime” means operationally. Check whether the device: Shows no charging indication; Charges only intermittently; Appears fully charged but shuts down quickly; Loses charge while powered off; Operates from external power but not from battery; Fails only when disconnected from the charger; Has significantly shorter runtime than comparable units; Shuts down when moved or when the power cable is disturbed. Expected: The complaint is converted into a reproducible symptom. Why it matters: Charging failure, poor battery capacity, loose power connection, and inaccurate charge indication are different failure paths.

steps.title: Inspect the Device and Power Accessories Externally
steps.instructions: With the scanner removed from patient use, inspect: AC power cord; External power supply or adapter; Low-voltage charging lead; Device power/charging receptacle; Cable strain-relief areas; Connector pins and contact surfaces; Battery compartment area, where externally accessible; Housing for evidence of impact or liquid intrusion. Look for: Loose connections; Bent or damaged contacts; Frayed wiring; Cracked insulation; Contamination; Corrosion; Unusual heat; Swelling; Burn odor. Expected: No visible condition explains unreliable charging or creates a safety concern. If damage, battery swelling, overheating, or burning odor is found, stop troubleshooting, remove the device from service, and escalate for repair.

steps.title: Verify the AC Source
steps.instructions: Connect the charger to a known-good AC receptacle. When appropriate, verify the receptacle using approved Clinical Engineering test practices or confirm operation with known-good equipment. Avoid assuming the scanner is defective based only on the originally reported outlet. Expected: Reliable AC power is available to the charging system. If the device begins charging normally on a verified outlet, the original power source or facility connection was the likely cause. Document the finding and stop.

steps.title: Reseat the Complete Charging Path
steps.instructions: Disconnect and firmly reconnect: AC cord to the power source; AC cord to the external power supply, when detachable; Power supply output lead to the scanner; Any accessible charging connection associated with the mounting arrangement. Observe whether the charging indication changes when the connection is reseated. Expected: Charging remains stable without requiring pressure, cable positioning, or repeated manipulation. Why it matters: A partially seated low-voltage charging connector can mimic a failed battery. A field report for this model family specifically describes apparent “battery not holding a charge” complaints associated with the charging cable not remaining connected, so Clinical Engineering should rule out the external charging path early. If reseating restores reliable charging, document the loose or incomplete connection and stop after verifying stable operation.

steps.title: Check for an Intermittent Cable or Connector Condition
steps.instructions: While observing the charging indication, gently check the external cable near: Power supply output; Strain relief; Device charging plug; Scanner receptacle. Do not force, sharply bend, or stress the connector. Expected: Charging status remains stable during normal cable positioning. If charging repeatedly drops out with normal movement, substitute an approved known-good power accessory when available. If the failure follows the cable or adapter, replace the defective accessory and stop after verification.

steps.title: Compare With a Known-Good Approved Power Supply or Charging Accessory
steps.instructions: When an identical approved accessory is available, substitute the known-good: AC cord; External power supply; Charging lead, as applicable to the configuration. Change one component at a time. Expected: The substitution identifies whether the failure follows an external power accessory. If the scanner charges normally with a known-good approved accessory, remove the failed accessory from service, replace it, verify charging, and stop. Do not substitute an unapproved adapter based only on connector fit.

steps.title: Observe Charging Behavior Over a Controlled Interval
steps.instructions: Connect the scanner to verified external power and record: Initial battery indication; Charging indication; Time charging begins; Whether the indication progresses; Whether charging stops unexpectedly; Any warning or abnormal message; Unusual heat from the device, battery area, or power supply. Expected: The device maintains a stable charging state and battery indication progresses appropriately. If no charging response occurs despite verified AC power and known-good external accessories, continue to the next step.

steps.title: Perform a Controlled Full-Charge and Runtime Evaluation
steps.instructions: For a short-runtime complaint, allow the device to charge fully according to the facility’s approved procedure and manufacturer guidance. Then disconnect external power and operate the scanner under a consistent, controlled bench-use condition. Record: Starting battery indication; Start time; Approximate workload; Time to low-battery indication; Time to shutdown, if safely evaluated; Any abrupt percentage drop or unexpected shutdown. Expected: Runtime is reasonably stable and appropriate for the condition and age of the battery. Why it matters: A battery may accept a charge indication but have insufficient usable capacity. If runtime is clearly poor compared with a known-good equivalent unit under similar conditions, suspect battery degradation.

steps.title: Inspect and Reseat the Battery Only When Externally Accessible and Authorized
steps.instructions: If the model configuration provides an externally serviceable battery and facility procedures permit it: Power the scanner off; Disconnect external power; Inspect the battery and accessible contacts; Check for contamination, damage, swelling, or abnormal heat; Reseat the battery securely. Do not open the battery pack or perform internal cell-level work. Expected: The battery is physically secure and recognized consistently. If reseating restores normal charging and runtime, complete verification and stop.

steps.title: Compare With a Known-Good Compatible Battery
steps.instructions: When available and permitted by Clinical Engineering procedures, install a known-good compatible battery intended for the BioCon 700 / 750 family. Medline lists a replacement battery accessory for both BioCon 700 and 750 bladder scanners. Expected: The substitution separates a degraded battery from a scanner-side charging problem. If the device charges and operates normally with the known-good battery: Remove the failed battery from service; Replace it with the correct compatible battery; Verify charging; Verify acceptable runtime; Complete final functional checks. Then stop.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Failure Stays With the Scanner
steps.instructions: If the issue persists with: Verified AC power; Secure charging connections; Known-good approved external power accessories; A known-good compatible battery; then the fault is more likely within the scanner’s charging, power-management, battery-recognition, or related internal circuitry. Expected: External and easily replaceable causes have been ruled out. Do not proceed into board-level troubleshooting unless specifically authorized, trained, and supported by current service documentation.

steps.title: Perform Final Functional Verification Before Return to Service
steps.instructions: After any corrective action: Confirm stable startup; Confirm external power operation; Confirm charging indication; Confirm battery recognition; Confirm operation after external power is disconnected; Confirm reasonable battery endurance; Confirm no abnormal heat, smell, or intermittent shutdown; Perform applicable facility functional checks. Expected: The scanner operates predictably from both the intended external power source and battery before return to clinical use. If verification fails, remove the device from service and escalate.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the BioCon 750 would show a charged battery but shut down shortly after being disconnected from external power.
CCR.Cause: Controlled runtime testing confirmed poor battery capacity, and the scanner operated normally with a known-good compatible replacement battery.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the degraded battery, installed the correct replacement battery, verified charging and battery operation, completed functional testing, and returned the scanner to service.

title: Medline BioCon 700 / 750 Series Bladder Scanner - Touchscreen or Display Failure
description: Troubleshooting a blank, frozen, dim, intermittent, distorted, or unresponsive touchscreen/display after external power, contamination, and startup causes are checked.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unresolved touchscreen or display problem while the bladder scanner is being relied upon for active patient assessment. If bladder-volume information is clinically needed, provide another verified bladder scanner or appropriate alternate assessment method before continuing. Expected: Patient care is not delayed or dependent on a device with unreliable visual controls or results. Why it matters: The BioCon 700 and 750 are bladder scanners, and available Medline product information identifies touchscreen display functionality as part of the device interface. An unreadable or unreliable interface can prevent dependable operation and interpretation. If patient care is safely transferred, continue troubleshooting in a controlled Clinical Engineering setting.

steps.title: Confirm the Exact Failure Behavior
steps.instructions: Power on the unit and determine whether the problem is: Completely blank display; Display illuminated but no usable image; Frozen screen; Touchscreen not responding; Touch response offset from the selected area; Only certain screen areas unresponsive; Flickering or intermittent image; Dim or unusually dark display; Distorted image, lines, or abnormal colors; Failure only during battery operation; Failure only while connected to external power. Expected: The complaint is narrowed to a display, touch-input, power-related, or intermittent condition. Do not treat “screen broken” as a complete diagnosis.

steps.title: Inspect for Physical Damage or Contamination
steps.instructions: With the unit removed from patient use, inspect the display and surrounding enclosure for: Cracked touchscreen surface; Impact marks; Separation or lifting at the display edge; Liquid intrusion evidence; Dried gel or cleaning residue; Heavy fingerprints or contamination; Damage near enclosure seams; Signs of a recent drop. Clean the touchscreen only with facility-approved methods compatible with the equipment. Expected: The screen is clean, dry, intact, and free of anything that could interfere with touch operation. If cleaning restores reliable touch response, verify full operation and stop.

steps.title: Remove External Touch Interference
steps.instructions: Remove any non-original item that may be affecting the touchscreen, including: Temporary protective film; Improvised screen covering; Labels overlapping the active display; Tape; Residue from disinfectant products; Objects resting against the screen. Expected: The touchscreen responds normally without mechanical or surface interference. If normal operation returns, document the cause and stop.

steps.title: Verify External Power and Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Check whether the failure occurs: On battery only; On AC/external power only; On both power sources. Inspect the external power adapter and accessible connections for looseness, damage, or intermittent contact. Medline lists power-adapter and battery accessories for the BioCon 700 and 750 family, supporting comparison of power-source behavior during troubleshooting. When appropriate, test a known-good compatible power source or known-good battery according to facility procedure. Expected: The display remains stable on a verified power source. If the issue occurs only with one battery or external power accessory and a known-good compatible substitute resolves it, replace or route the failed accessory appropriately and stop.

steps.title: Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: If the display is frozen or touch input is unresponsive: Ensure the unit is not supporting patient care; Perform a normal shutdown if controls remain functional; Allow the shutdown to complete; Restart the device; Observe the entire startup sequence. Expected: The unit boots normally and the touchscreen becomes responsive. If the issue clears after restart, do not immediately assume permanent repair. Repeat operation sufficiently to determine whether the problem recurs.

steps.title: Observe the Startup Sequence Carefully
steps.instructions: During startup, determine whether: The display never illuminates; A startup image appears and then disappears; The screen freezes at a repeatable point; The image is normal but touch input fails; Touch works initially and then stops; The unit appears to operate despite a blank display; A diagnostic, maintenance, or hardware warning appears. Expected: The failure point helps distinguish a total display problem from touch-input failure, startup lockup, or broader system malfunction. The BioCon 750 is described as having self-diagnostic capability, so any displayed hardware or maintenance indication should be recorded exactly rather than cleared and ignored.

steps.title: Test Touch Response Across the Entire Active Screen
steps.instructions: Using normal, non-destructive operation, test multiple accessible areas of the touchscreen. Check whether: All areas respond; One edge does not respond; A specific region is dead; The selected item differs from the touched location; Touch input activates without being touched; Response is delayed or intermittent. Expected: Touch response is consistent across the usable interface. A repeatable dead region, offset touch response, or phantom input strongly supports escalation rather than continued external troubleshooting.

steps.title: Check for Temperature or Environmental Influence
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint began after: Storage in a hot location; Storage in a cold location; Transport between substantially different environments; Exposure to condensation; Recent cleaning with excessive fluid. Allow the device to stabilize in the normal operating environment before retesting when appropriate. Expected: The display and touchscreen operate consistently under normal environmental conditions. If the issue resolves only temporarily and returns repeatedly, do not consider the device reliable.

steps.title: Gently Check for Reproducible Intermittency
steps.instructions: Without opening the enclosure or stressing the unit, observe whether the failure occurs during: Normal repositioning; Movement on the cart or stand; Connection or removal of external power; Transition between battery and external power; Routine handling. Do not strike, twist, flex, or intentionally shock the equipment. Expected: The screen remains stable during normal handling. If the display flickers, blanks, freezes, or changes during ordinary movement, remove the unit from service for bench evaluation.

steps.title: Compare With Known-Good Compatible External Components
steps.instructions: Where available and permitted, substitute only compatible known-good external items relevant to the observed condition, such as: Power adapter; Battery; External power cord or approved detachable component. Medline lists accessories specifically for BioCon 700 and 750 scanners, so compatibility should be confirmed rather than assumed. Expected: The failure either follows an external component or remains with the scanner. If a known-good external component resolves the issue consistently, replace or route the failed component appropriately and stop.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Failure Is Persistent or Intermittent
steps.instructions: Repeat startup and normal interface checks enough to establish whether the issue is: Fully resolved; Repeatable; Intermittent; Triggered by power-source changes; Triggered by normal movement; Limited to specific touchscreen regions. Expected: Clinical Engineering has a reproducible description of the failure before escalation. Do not return the unit to service solely because an intermittent display fault temporarily disappeared.

steps.title: Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: If the issue appears resolved, verify normal device operation according to facility procedure and applicable manufacturer requirements. Confirm: Display is readable; Touch input is accurate; No dead screen regions are present; Startup completes normally; Device remains stable on intended power sources; No diagnostic or hardware warnings remain; Normal scanning workflow can be completed safely. Expected: The device demonstrates stable, repeatable operation. If any display or touchscreen abnormality remains, stop troubleshooting and escalate.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the BioCon 750 touchscreen intermittently froze and stopped responding during bladder scanning setup.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found heavy dried residue across the touchscreen surface; touch response returned normally after approved cleaning and remained stable during repeated functional checks.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned the touchscreen using the approved method, restarted the scanner, verified touch response across the active display, and completed functional testing with no recurrence.

helpfulDetails: Outlet or external power source tested
Screen blank, frozen, dim, or distorted
Failure during startup or after boot

title: Medline BioCon 700 / 750 Series Bladder Scanner - Printer / Paper Feed Failure
description: Troubleshooting absent printing, blank output, paper feed failure, jams, or intermittent printer operation caused by paper loading, consumables, obstruction, or printer faults.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unresolved printer problem while the scanner is actively being used for patient assessment. Complete or repeat any clinically necessary bladder measurement using a verified device, then move the affected scanner to a controlled Clinical Engineering area. Expected: Patient assessment is not delayed by printer troubleshooting. Why it matters: The printer supports documentation, while the BioCon device itself is used for noninvasive bladder-volume assessment. Clinical needs should be addressed before extended equipment evaluation. If removing the device from use resolves the immediate clinical concern, continue troubleshooting off patient.

steps.title: 2. Verify the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Power on the scanner and reproduce the complaint using a controlled test. Determine whether the printer: Produces no response; Makes operating noise but does not feed paper; Feeds paper but prints blank; Feeds intermittently; Skews or bunches the paper; Jams during output; Prints faintly or incompletely; Fails only after a specific scan or print command. Observe any displayed message, unusual sound, or abnormal printer behavior. Expected: The failure is narrowed to command, feed, paper-path, or print-quality behavior. If printing operates normally and repeatedly during testing, document the unable-to-duplicate condition and inspect consumable loading before return to service.

steps.title: 3. Verify Scanner Power and General Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm the BioCon scanner: Powers on normally; Completes startup without an unresolved fault; Maintains stable power; Responds normally to controls; Can perform the basic non-patient workflow needed to generate printable information. For intermittent complaints, test with a known-good power source or adequately charged battery as appropriate. Expected: The scanner remains stable during the print attempt. If the entire device resets, freezes, or loses power during printing, stop treating the problem as a simple paper-feed complaint and evaluate the broader power or system fault separately.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Paper Supply
steps.instructions: Open the printer access area and inspect the installed roll without disassembling the printer mechanism. Check for: Empty roll; Nearly depleted roll; Crushed or deformed roll; Damp paper; Contaminated paper; Torn paper edge; Paper installed off-center; Roll binding against the compartment; Incorrect paper dimensions. Use compatible thermal paper intended for the BioCon scanner configuration. Compatible thermal paper is specifically marketed for the BioCon 700 and 750 families. Expected: Paper is clean, correctly sized, free-moving, and properly seated. If replacing a damaged or incorrect roll restores consistent printing, the issue is resolved. Stop.

steps.title: 5. Verify Thermal Paper Orientation
steps.instructions: If paper advances but the output is blank, verify that the thermal-sensitive side is oriented correctly for the printer. A practical controlled check is to lightly mark both sides of a removed paper sample with a fingernail or another non-damaging blunt edge. Thermal coating typically darkens from friction on the active side. Reload the roll so the printable surface faces the thermal print mechanism. Expected: Printed content becomes visible. If correcting paper orientation restores normal output, the issue is resolved. Stop.

steps.title: 6. Reload the Paper From Scratch
steps.instructions: Remove the roll and reload it carefully. Confirm: Roll sits squarely; Paper unwinds without binding; Leading edge is straight rather than torn diagonally; Paper follows the intended exit path; Cover closes fully without pinching the paper; Adequate paper extends through the exit before testing. Do not force the cover closed against a misaligned roll. Expected: Paper advances straight through the exit path. If proper reloading restores normal operation, the issue is resolved. Stop.

steps.title: 7. Inspect the External Paper Path for Obstruction
steps.instructions: With the device removed from patient use and powered down as appropriate, inspect only readily accessible areas of the paper path. Look for: Torn paper fragments; Folded paper; Adhesive residue; Dirt or debris; Foreign material; Paper wrapped around an accessible roller; A damaged or obstructed exit slot. Use only safe external cleaning methods consistent with facility and manufacturer requirements. Do not probe deeply into the mechanism or force printer components. Expected: The accessible paper path is clear. If removal of an obvious accessible obstruction restores reliable feed, repeat several print tests. If successful, stop.

steps.title: 8. Inspect the Printer Cover and Latching
steps.instructions: Check whether the printer door or cover: Closes completely; Sits flush; Remains latched; Shows cracks or distortion; Allows the roll to remain properly positioned. A cover that does not seat correctly may prevent proper paper pressure or alignment. Expected: The printer compartment closes securely without excessive force. If reseating the cover restores reliable feed and printing, the issue is resolved. Stop.

steps.title: 9. Test With a Known-Good Compatible Paper Roll
steps.instructions: Install a fresh, known-good compatible thermal paper roll. This helps separate: Paper-related failure; Incorrect consumable; Deformed roll; Moisture damage; Coating/orientation problem; Actual printer mechanism fault. Medline-compatible paper products are listed for BioCon scanner families, including the 700 and 750. Expected: The printer feeds and produces readable output. If a known-good roll resolves the issue, replace the defective consumable and stop.

steps.title: 10. Compare Feed Behavior With Print Behavior
steps.instructions: Run repeated controlled print attempts and observe the mechanism. No motor or feed response. Possible causes include: Print command not reaching the printer; Printer not being activated by the system; Electrical printer fault; Internal connection fault; Printer assembly failure. Motor sound but no paper movement. Possible causes include: Paper binding; Feed roller problem; Mechanical obstruction; Loss of roller engagement. Paper moves but output is blank. Possible causes include: Reversed thermal paper; Incorrect paper; Thermal printhead issue; Printer drive/electrical fault. Paper skews or jams repeatedly. Possible causes include: Incorrect loading; Damaged roll; Debris; Feed alignment problem; Worn mechanism. Expected: The observed behavior points to either an external correctable cause or a persistent printer fault. Do not assume internal failure until consumable, loading, and accessible paper-path causes have been ruled out.

steps.title: 11. Reproduce the Failure Multiple Times
steps.instructions: After correcting any external issue, perform several consecutive print tests. Verify: Print command is accepted; Paper advances each time; Output is readable; Paper remains centered; No abnormal grinding or clicking occurs; No jam recurs; Device remains stable. Expected: Printing is repeatable, not merely successful once. If repeated tests pass, document the corrective action and final functional status. Stop.

steps.title: 12. Stop Before Internal Printer Repair
steps.instructions: If the printer still: Does not respond; Repeatedly jams with correctly loaded known-good paper; Produces blank output with verified paper orientation; Makes abnormal mechanical noise; Fails intermittently after external causes are eliminated; Shows visible printer mechanism damage, do not proceed into unsupported printer disassembly or internal board-level troubleshooting. Expected: The device is escalated appropriately rather than subjected to unnecessary invasive repair.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the BioCon 750 printer would not feed paper after a bladder scan.
CCR.Cause: Found the thermal paper roll misaligned in the printer compartment, causing the leading edge to bind at the exit path.
CCR.Resolution: Removed and correctly reloaded the compatible thermal paper, cleared the accessible paper path, and verified five consecutive print cycles with normal feed and readable output.

helpfulDetails: Battery and/or external power behavior checked

title: Medline BioCon 700 / 750 Series Bladder Scanner - Inaccurate Bladder Volume or Poor Targeting
description: Troubleshooting inaccurate, inconsistent, or unexpected bladder-volume results caused by targeting, probe technique, gel, settings, patient factors, accessories, or device faults.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot questionable bladder-volume measurements while clinical decisions are being based solely on the affected scanner. If urinary retention or another time-sensitive condition is suspected, provide clinical staff with another verified assessment method or known-good bladder scanner before continuing. Expected: Patient care is not dependent on an unverified bladder-volume result. Why it matters: The BioCon series uses noninvasive ultrasound to estimate bladder volume. Poor targeting or unreliable measurements can produce misleading results and should not delay appropriate clinical assessment. The BioCon 700 includes real-time pre-scan capability intended to help locate the bladder before measurement, while the BioCon 750 uses BladderPoint targeting technology. If patient safety is restored, continue troubleshooting in a controlled Clinical Engineering setting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Problem
steps.instructions: Determine what “inaccurate” or “poor targeting” means in practice: Repeated scans produce widely different volumes; Measured volume does not correlate with expected clinical findings; Scanner repeatedly fails to locate the bladder; Targeting indicator remains off-center; Bladder image is weak, incomplete, or difficult to identify; Measurements are consistently unexpectedly low; Measurements are consistently unexpectedly high; Problem occurs only with certain patients; Problem occurs with all patients or test conditions. Repeat the complaint only under safe conditions and document the actual displayed volume, targeting behavior, and any messages. Expected: The failure pattern is clearly defined. If the issue cannot be reproduced and repeated scans are stable: document findings and stop after completing appropriate functional verification.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Probe and Scan Surface
steps.instructions: Examine the ultrasound probe for: Cracks; Impact damage; Separation of the probe housing; Damage to the acoustic surface; Dried gel buildup; Residue or contamination; Evidence of fluid intrusion; Abnormal looseness. Clean the probe only using approved methods and compatible products. Expected: The acoustic surface is clean, intact, and suitable for consistent ultrasound coupling. Why it matters: Physical damage or contamination at the probe surface can interfere with acoustic transmission and contribute to weak or inconsistent targeting. If cleaning resolves the issue: repeat several scans for consistency, document the correction, and stop.

steps.title: 4. Verify Adequate Ultrasound Gel
steps.instructions: Confirm that sufficient compatible ultrasound gel is being used between the probe and test surface or patient. Look for: Too little gel; Dried gel; Large air gaps; Uneven probe contact; Inappropriate substitute products. Apply fresh ultrasound gel and repeat the scan. Expected: The probe maintains continuous acoustic coupling without visible air gaps. Why it matters: Air between the transducer and skin significantly interferes with ultrasound transmission and can cause poor image quality or failed targeting. If fresh gel restores consistent targeting and volume readings: the problem is resolved; stop.

steps.title: 5. Verify Probe Position and Orientation
steps.instructions: Confirm that the probe is positioned according to the device’s intended suprapubic scanning approach and that the probe orientation is correct. For bench evaluation, determine whether the complaint may be caused by: Starting too far above the pubic region; Aiming away from the expected bladder location; Excessive probe angulation; Repeated repositioning before the device completes its scan; Incorrect orientation of the probe marker or handle; Excessive pressure that changes probe position. The BioCon 700 supports real-time pre-scan viewing to assist bladder location, while the BioCon 750 is marketed with BladderPoint technology that provides a targeting reference for locating the bladder. Expected: The displayed targeting aid or bladder image can be centered consistently before measurement. If corrected positioning restores repeatable measurements: document the technique-related cause and stop.

steps.title: 6. Check Whether the Problem Is Patient-Specific
steps.instructions: Determine whether poor targeting occurs: On one patient only; On a particular body habitus; After recent voiding; With very low expected bladder volume; With abdominal dressings or wounds; With scars near the scan area; With unusual pelvic anatomy; With conditions that may complicate ultrasound interpretation. Do not conclude that the scanner is defective from a single difficult scan. Expected: Clinical Engineering distinguishes a device-wide failure from patient-specific scanning difficulty. Why it matters: Bladder scanners estimate volume from ultrasound data, and anatomy or scan conditions may affect targeting and repeatability.

steps.title: 7. Verify Patient or Scan-Mode Settings
steps.instructions: Review applicable patient-selection or scan settings before testing. Confirm that the selected mode matches the intended patient category and available device options. Pay particular attention to sex-related settings where applicable. Guidance for the BioCon 700 indicates that female-mode selection may account for the presence of the uterus, while adult patients without a uterus are directed to the male setting in the referenced BioCon guidance. Do not change settings solely to force a desired volume result. Expected: The scanner is configured appropriately for the test condition. If correcting an inappropriate setting restores consistent results: document the configuration issue and stop.

steps.title: 8. Compare Repeated Measurements
steps.instructions: Under controlled conditions, obtain several consecutive scans without substantially changing: Probe position; Probe angle; Test subject or phantom; Gel application; Device settings. Record each displayed volume. Look for: Tight clustering of values; Large unexplained variation; Intermittent zero or near-zero results; Loss of targeting between scans; Results that change when the cable or probe is moved. Expected: Repeated measurements are reasonably consistent for the same controlled condition. If repeatability is acceptable: investigate technique, patient factors, or the original clinical environment before assuming device failure.

steps.title: 9. Compare With a Known-Good Scanner When Available
steps.instructions: Using the same safe test condition, compare the affected BioCon with another verified bladder scanner. Keep variables as consistent as practical: Same test condition; Similar probe location; Similar patient or phantom state; Fresh gel; Appropriate settings. Do not expect two different bladder scanners to display perfectly identical values. Expected: The affected unit should not show gross, persistent, or unexplained disagreement across repeated controlled comparisons. If only the affected unit remains inconsistent: continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: 10. Inspect the Probe Cable and Connections
steps.instructions: Where applicable to the specific BioCon configuration, inspect the probe cable and connection path for: Loose connection; Partially seated connector; Bent or damaged contacts; Crushed cable; Sharp kinks; Intermittent response during gentle cable movement; Strain near the probe or connector. Power the device down before disconnecting or reconnecting accessories when required by local procedure. Reconnect securely and retest. Expected: The probe connection is mechanically secure and scanning remains stable during normal handling. If reseating the connection resolves the issue: repeat functional checks, document the correction, and stop.

steps.title: 11. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Probe When Authorized
steps.instructions: If your department has an approved compatible known-good probe, substitute it without opening the scanner. Repeat the same controlled scan comparison. Expected: If the known-good probe restores repeatability, suspect the original probe or cable assembly. If the problem remains unchanged, suspect the console, configuration, calibration state, or another device-level fault. Do not condemn the console before ruling out the external probe assembly. If the replacement probe resolves the issue: remove the defective probe from service and follow local replacement or repair procedures.

steps.title: 12. Review Self-Diagnostic or Maintenance Indications
steps.instructions: Check for: Hardware warnings; Maintenance messages; Self-diagnostic failures; Startup abnormalities; Persistent error indications; Abnormal touchscreen or display behavior. The BioCon 750 is marketed with built-in self-diagnostic capability intended to identify hardware or maintenance concerns. Document the exact message rather than writing only “scanner error.” Expected: No unresolved diagnostic condition is present. If a persistent hardware or maintenance indication appears: stop routine troubleshooting and escalate for service evaluation.

steps.title: 13. Evaluate Calibration or Accuracy Verification Status
steps.instructions: Review: Last preventive maintenance date; Last accuracy verification; Previous repair history; Prior probe replacement; Recent impact or drop event; Repeated inaccurate-volume complaints; Applicable calibration or verification requirements. Medline lists a calibration kit accessory specifically for the BioCon 700, supporting the need to consider formal verification when accuracy remains questionable. Do not improvise calibration procedures or adjust internal values without approved service documentation, proper test equipment, and authorization. Expected: The scanner’s verification status is current and traceable. If accuracy cannot be verified: remove the unit from clinical use pending proper evaluation.

steps.title: 14. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Before returning the unit to service, verify: Scanner powers on normally; Probe is recognized and physically intact; Targeting or pre-scan function operates; Repeated scans are reasonably consistent; No unresolved diagnostic message is present; Controls and display operate normally; Device passes applicable local inspection or performance checks. Expected: The scanner demonstrates stable, repeatable operation with no unresolved safety or accuracy concern. If the device passes: return it to service according to department policy and document the findings.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the BioCon bladder scanner produced inconsistent bladder volumes and was difficult to target despite repeated scans.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found inadequate acoustic coupling from dried gel residue on the probe surface and insufficient fresh ultrasound gel during repeat testing.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned the probe using approved methods, applied fresh ultrasound gel, repeated controlled scans with consistent targeting and repeatable volume measurements, and returned the device to service.

title: Medline BioCon 900S Bladder Scanner - Wireless Scanner Not Communicating
description: Troubleshooting failed or intermittent wireless communication caused by power, alignment, obstruction, contamination, settings, receiver-side connections, or persistent communication faults.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unresolved communication problem while the BioCon 900S is being relied upon for active patient assessment. If scan results are required for immediate clinical decision-making, provide another verified bladder scanner or approved alternate assessment method before continuing. Expected: Patient care is not delayed or dependent on equipment with unreliable communication. If moving to another device resolves the immediate clinical concern, continue troubleshooting only in a controlled Clinical Engineering setting.

steps.title: Confirm the Exact Communication Failure
steps.instructions: Determine what staff mean by “not communicating.” Check whether: The scanner powers on normally; Scanning functions locally; Results appear on the scanner; Data fail to transfer to the receiving component; Communication is intermittent; Failure occurs only in one location; Failure occurs only with one charger, cradle, workstation, or accessory; An error message or abnormal indicator is present. Expected: The failure is narrowed to scanner operation, data transfer, receiving equipment, or an intermittent connection problem. Do not assume the scanner itself has failed until the receiving side is also checked.

steps.title: Verify Scanner Power and Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm that the scanner: Powers on normally; Completes startup; Shows adequate battery charge; Does not reboot or shut down unexpectedly; Does not display abnormal battery behavior. Charge the scanner fully using the approved charging equipment if battery status is questionable. Expected: The scanner remains powered and stable throughout communication testing. Why it matters: Low or unstable power can produce intermittent behavior that may be reported as a communication fault. If restoring a stable charge resolves communication, document the battery or charging condition and stop.

steps.title: Inspect the Scanner and Communication Areas Externally
steps.instructions: Examine the scanner for: Cracked housing; Evidence of impact or drop damage; Fluid intrusion; Heavy contamination; Damaged display; Loose external components; Debris over communication windows or sensor areas. Clean only according to approved device cleaning practices. Expected: No physical damage, contamination, or obstruction is found that could interfere with normal operation. If cleaning an obstructed communication area restores reliable transfer, verify repeated operation and stop.

steps.title: Verify Infrared Communication Alignment
steps.instructions: The BioCon 900S communication path should be treated as line-of-sight infrared communication rather than conventional room-wide Wi-Fi. Position the scanner and receiving communication area as intended and verify: Communication windows face the correct direction; The scanner is properly seated or positioned; No labels, tape, covers, carts, hands, or accessories block the path; The scanner is not significantly misaligned; The test is performed at an appropriate close range. Expected: Communication succeeds when the infrared path is properly aligned and unobstructed. If proper alignment restores communication, document misalignment or obstruction as the cause and stop.

steps.title: Clean the Communication Windows
steps.instructions: Inspect the applicable infrared communication surfaces for: Fingerprints; Dried disinfectant residue; Ultrasound gel; Dust; Adhesive residue; Scratches or clouding. Clean approved external surfaces using a compatible method and allow them to dry before retesting. Expected: Communication surfaces are clean, dry, and unobstructed. If cleaning restores repeatable communication, perform multiple transfers before returning the device to service.

steps.title: Check the Charger, Cradle, or Receiving Component
steps.instructions: Inspect the receiving side of the communication path. Verify: AC power is present where required; Power indicators are normal; The approved power supply is connected securely; The scanner is positioned correctly relative to the receiving component; No connector is loose; No visible damage is present; Communication surfaces are clean. Expected: The receiving component is powered, physically intact, and ready to communicate. If restoring power or correcting the receiving-side setup resolves the issue, verify repeated communication and stop.

steps.title: Reseat Accessible External Connections
steps.instructions: Power down equipment as appropriate and reseat accessible external connections associated with the receiving system. Check: Power adapter connections; USB connections, if used in the local configuration; Workstation-side cables; External accessory connections. Do not open the scanner or perform internal disassembly. Expected: All external connections are fully seated and mechanically secure. If reseating a connection restores communication, perform a movement check and repeated transfer test before stopping.

steps.title: Restart Both Sides of the Communication Path
steps.instructions: Perform a controlled restart of: The BioCon 900S scanner; The associated receiving component or workstation, when applicable. Allow each component to complete startup before retesting communication. Expected: Temporary software or initialization problems clear and communication resumes normally. If restart restores communication, repeat the transfer several times to confirm the problem is not immediately recurring.

steps.title: Verify Device Settings and Intended Workflow
steps.instructions: Review accessible settings related to communication and data handling. Confirm: The correct workflow is being used; Patient or scan data are being saved as expected; No unintended setup change occurred; The receiving component is operating in the expected mode; The problem is not limited to one operator sequence. Do not alter protected service settings without approved documentation. Expected: Configuration and workflow are appropriate for the installed system. If correcting an accessible setting restores communication, document the setting found and stop.

steps.title: Test in a Controlled Environment
steps.instructions: Move the scanner and associated receiving equipment to a controlled Clinical Engineering test area. Repeat communication testing away from: Strong direct sunlight; Unusual infrared sources; Physical obstructions; Crowded equipment arrangements; The original clinical location. Expected: Communication behavior is reproducible independent of the care location. If communication works reliably in the test area but fails in the original location, investigate environmental interference, positioning, or site-specific receiving equipment before condemning the scanner.

steps.title: Compare With a Known-Good Compatible Component
steps.instructions: When available and permitted by your support configuration, compare using known-good compatible equipment. Examples: Test the affected scanner with a known-good receiving component; Test a known-good scanner with the suspected receiving component. Change only one variable at a time. Expected: The failure follows either the scanner or the receiving side. Why it matters: Controlled substitution is one of the strongest ways to isolate an external communication problem without internal disassembly. If the failure clearly follows one component, remove that component from service and stop.

steps.title: Run Accessible Self-Test or Functional Checks
steps.instructions: Use only approved, accessible diagnostic or self-test functions available to Clinical Engineering. Document: Pass/fail result; Any displayed fault; Whether probe/scanner functions pass while communication fails; Whether the fault is repeatable after restart. Expected: The unit either passes functional checks or produces evidence supporting escalation. Do not enter undocumented service modes or perform internal repair based solely on assumption.

steps.title: Perform a Final Repeatability Test
steps.instructions: After any corrective action, verify: Scanner startup; Stable battery operation; Successful scan acquisition; Successful communication or transfer; Multiple consecutive communication attempts; Normal operation after repositioning or reseating. Expected: Communication remains reliable across repeated tests. If the issue is resolved and repeatable operation is confirmed, return the device to service according to department policy and stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Medline BioCon 900S scanner powered on and completed scans but would not communicate with the receiving system.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found contamination and misalignment at the infrared communication path, preventing reliable data transfer.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned the external communication surfaces, corrected scanner alignment, and verified multiple consecutive successful scan transfers; device returned to service.
